beats.say: In seventeen oh seven, four Royal Navy ships sailed straight into the rocks off Scilly. Two thousand men drowned in a single night.
Not from war. From not knowing where they were.
Latitude was easy, the sun gives it away. Longitude, how far east or west you are, was invisible. Half of every map was guesswork.

visual.def: how far east or west you are — the one thing no sailor could measure.

beats.say: But longitude is secretly just time. Note noon where you are. Compare it with the clock back home. Every hour of difference is fifteen degrees of the globe.
The catch: no clock on Earth could keep time on a rolling, salt soaked ship. So in seventeen fourteen, Parliament offered twenty thousand pounds, millions today, to anyone who could.
The Royal Society expected an astronomer to win it. They got a self taught village carpenter named John Harrison.
Harrison spent thirty one years building four clocks, each stranger and smaller than the last.
The first was the size of a dresser. The last, after three decades of obsession, fit in a coat pocket.
On its Atlantic trial, H4 drifted five seconds in eighty one days at sea. The astronomers' best method missed by miles.
The committee stalled for decades before paying the carpenter. But he had already solved the ocean. Every GPS satellite still runs on his idea. Position is time.
